Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher/terrible installation instructions ] || ---------------- || We were looking for a quiet dishwasher. This one certainly meets that goal. The only time we can really hear it is when it drains, and that's not the dishwasher's fault but due to the existing plumbing into the drain via the sink. We installed the unit ourselves. The installation instructions are poorly organized, somewhat confusing, and not what I would have expected based on prior installations in the past of former dishwashers or other GE appliances. The additional soundproofing that goes on the flange the front door abuts could not be used; there was insufficient room to get the dishwasher into its under-cabinet space if the side pieces were used (the top piece was used). The front door as delivered is a bit askew, and we will be contacting GE to see if there is an adjustment to get it flush/parallel with the washbasin's tub flange. The bulk of the owner's manual is for installation; we are still figuring out its use, but in general we are happy with the purchase. The four stars are principally due to the poorly organized installation instructions; the washer itself may (after some more usage) warrant five stars, but as they want this review as we are registering the unit, it's too soon to tell.

The smart app is a lot more useful than I thought it would be. I load dirty dishes in the dishwasher throughout the day and at night when I've already gone to my room, I can start the cycle right from my bed (I preload the detergent in the slot). I can't speak on behalf of the longevity but I hope it lasts a long time!

Sentence (English): Bought this unit DW80R5061US and it worked fine for the first month.
Comments (English): [ Poor Design ] || ---------------- || Bought this unit DW80R5061US and it worked fine for the first month. After that the unit progressively got worse with its ability to clean dishes. There are two main issues with this design; filtration and the wash arms.First, the filtration system is junk. Unlike other brands, there is no easy way of cleaning the filter! You have to remove 15 Robertson screws to get to the upper pump area at the bottom of the wash tub. If some young wiz kid designer built this to save energy so you should never have to clean the filter, then the system should have a self cleaning function. Why is this an issue, I have food particles sticking to glassware, hardly washes the second row and useless for the third.Now, I've followed the "recommended" procedures (hot water/good water flow; high end dish soap/lots of high end rinse agent; it's level; it's loaded properly per the manual… everything Samsung has suggested). I've had older/other models where you could throw the carcass with the pan of Thanksgiving dinner and the pan would be spotless. This unit can't wash dried-on egg from forks and leaves so much food grit on glasses I might as well wash the dishes by hand. The middle wash wand is focused down so anything on the flimsy second rack gets little; apparently depending on the bottom wand to reach the 2nd level.The second issue has hinted above, the third rack is basically useless. It hardly washes anything on the 3rd row and as mentioned the second upper wand points most of its power down to the bottom rack. The adjustable rack is so flimsy you can barely put in a large coffee cup.Before Samsung support tells me how "sorry they are", maybe you should rebate customers to buy your newest, more improved version before telling me this is a "rare occurrence"; since your testing was with clean plates. Geez your video states NOT use ever hole in the cutlery rack (never been an issue with older models). If you painstakingly use the 3rd upper rack for just cutlery, your 2nd rack doesn't get enough wash coming down. I suspect the issue is pump pressure and the tiny water heater to get to sanitize temp.With that said, if you put a mid-size load (properly loaded so dirty dishes face the middle/centre of the dishwasher), then use the storm-wash, full sanitize, high temp, it takes nearly 4 hrs to wash a load. And having to re-wash loads isn't saving any money, water or the climate.So having Canadian Thanksgiving we had to wash brunch for 6 people (4 hrs), dinner (2 loads @ 4 hrs) and the dishes were hit and miss. I hope the new fridge and stove I bought as a bundle last longer. This is a lemon of a design.

Sentence (English): I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores.
Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

Sentence (English): Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :)
Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

Sentence (English): I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient.
Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. Comments (English): [ Minix dishwasher accident, quality of life goes up vertically. ] || ---------------- || I'd always been confident I could live comfortably without a dishwasher, but with my baby due next month, I decided to get one to ease the burden of household chores. I've talked to people online and with friends, and they tell me they can't communicate with people who don't. They tell me they can never go back to a life without a dishwasher. I was agonizing over it until I saw a Minix dishwasher on Coupang, so I bought it right away. There are plenty of other brands in a similar price range, but Minix's greatest strength is its no-drill, no-installation design. Since we don't live in our own home, ^^, products that require drilling holes or direct plumbing were a bit burdensome. I also didn't like the fact that the dishwasher was so big. This one is the perfect size for a two-person household (three when the baby arrives next month). It takes up just the right amount of space on the countertop. Installation was so easy that I was 33 weeks pregnant and was able to carry it all up and install it by myself. :) I received it yesterday and used it twice, and I'm very satisfied with its cleaning power. I also really like the bottom-mounted water supply. I've read reviews of other dishwashers and heard that most mini dishwashers have their water tanks located at the top, which is incredibly inconvenient. ^^ I've also seen reviews where some people pull the sink faucet to directly fill the water tank in their Minix dishwasher, so I tried that and it's even more convenient! I definitely feel like it uses less water than washing dishes by hand. I timed it with a stopwatch, and it took about 50 seconds with the water running at full strength to fill the recommended 6.5 liters. It's ridiculous to think that washing dishes by hand takes over 15 minutes! Touching the warm dishes after they've been thoroughly cleaned with just a little water and dried with hot air is incredibly satisfying. The catalog that came with the product included a note from the Minix CEO, which stated the company's mission: "To create a world where everyone can enjoy everything, even in small spaces." I was truly impressed. I've read it countless times. Minix's mission of enabling everyone to enjoy a leisurely home life without spatial constraints resonates with me so much that I want to join the company :) I'm actively promoting it to my friends who live in monthly rent ^^ I hope many people can enjoy this benefit. *Made in Korea!

The operation via the control panel on the top of the door is well thought out and works perfectly. The number of programs is very satisfactory. I'm currently using the automatic program where the dishwasher has learned from previous dishwashing cycles and applies this knowledge to the new cycles. Comments (Original): [ Sehr hochwertiger und smarter Geschirrspüler! ] || ---------------- || Habe das Gerät bereits seit mehreren Wochen im täglichen Einsatz.Der Beladungsprozess ist aufgrund der durchdachten und flexiblen Körbe und der Möglichkeiten diese in der Anordnung der Halteelemente zu verändern sehr simpel und schnell. Sentence (English): Overall, we felt this was a disappointing purchase.
Comments (English): [ Would Not Recommend This Model ] || ---------------- || Overall, we felt this was a disappointing purchase. I understand it's one of the lower-tier models, but based on recommendations for Bosch, we thought the quality would be better. Pros: it's very quiet when it runs. Cons: the dishes NEVER dry. We have tried the Extra Dry and Sanitize options as suggested, along with rinse aids, and the dishes still are slightly wet when the cycle is done. The 2nd con is the interior layout of the tines. Because of the layout and how closely the tines are set together on the bottom rack, we can't fit nearly as many items in this dishwasher as our previous washer. It's like the designers only designed this for a bunch of large dinner plates. And on the top rack, the spacing is too wide, allowing items to fall through. The entire unit feels flimsy and not durable. While this unit looks nicer than our previous washer, I don't see it standing the test of time.
